lines.text: Midnight in the Brass Cellar. Someone is tuning a cello very quietly, which in Port Murmur now counts as a protest.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: There you are, kid. Fresh from the press, still warm.
She drops a stack of posters on the piano. CONCERT. SATURDAY. YOU KNOW WHERE. Below the words, a very large trumpet.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (That trumpet looks a lot like mine. That trumpet looks a lot like evidence.)

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Six good walls between here and the tram stop. Four posters at least, or nobody hears about Saturday.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Um. What happens if the Squad sees me gluing?

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: They won't, if you keep to the dark. Their torches only reach so far, and a kid in a shadow is just a shadow.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: The lamps are another story. Under a lamp, you're on a stage. Glue fast.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (Stay in the dark. Stand still for ages. Also, somehow, be fast.)

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: And sound carries at night. One note out there and half the street hears it, Squad included.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: I didn't say that. I said everyone hears it.
Up the stairs, through the door with no handle, the streets wait: gray, still, and very well lit in all the wrong places.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: One more thing. The Squad parks a van on Market Row every night, under the brightest lamp in town. Lovely clean paint.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Are you... telling me to do something to it?

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: I'm telling you it's there. What you do with the spare paint is your business.
